panels.description: Wide, full page width. Pre-dawn, the sky the grey of old iron. A small party of riders leaving through the gate of Padmini Amma's estate. Padmini at the head, side saddle on a compact horse. Nagoji a little behind and to her left. Ibrahim Marakkar (short coat over a vest with bulging pockets, scar from his LEFT ear to his jaw) and two of Padmini's male relatives following: Nair men, bare-chested, white mundu hitched to the knee, hair knotted high at the front, no turbans.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Padmini Amma was taking me to be weighed.

panels.description: Wide landscape, morning mist lifting. The road winds inland through low green hills. Lotus leaves on a pond. An ancient tree with a small shrine at its foot, cloth bundles and oil lamps on its trunk. Women with baskets on their hips heading for the pepper gardens. In the foreground, children racing along a narrow bund between flooded channels. The riders small in the middle distance.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Their feet were sure on ridges that would have sent me tumbling into the channels.

panels.description: Medium two-shot, riding. Padmini (fifties, lined face) in cream silk with a narrow gold border, hitched for riding, simple gold at throat and wrists, thick black hair coiled at the nape, a sword with a worn leather-wrapped hilt at her right side, her long walking stick strapped along the saddle. She does not turn her head to speak. Nagoji in his commander's clothes: rust-red turban, cream tunic with the sleeves down to the wrists, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots, talwar. Thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, gold ear stud.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: You have heard of Velinadu. What did your hills tell you?

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Stories. Of company men who thought themselves safe until women closed the gates on them.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Of queens who could sign treaties without asking anyone's permission.

panels.description: Padmini in profile, lifting her chin toward the road ahead. The faintest smile.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Stories travel badly. But the bones of that one are not wrong.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Remember that when you meet Revathi. She carries those bones in her tongue.

panels.description: Wide, full width. Velinadu Kovilakam ahead. No towering walls, no bastions: a low ring of red laterite and earth circling a cluster of tiled roofs and broad trees. The gate is wide enough for carts and elephants. Nair guards (bare-chested, white mundu hitched to the knee, hair knotted high at the front, no turbans) with spears and small round shields watch the riders come. Seen from the approaching riders: no riders in frame.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Velinadu Kovilakam was not the city my Deccan mind had expected.

panels.description: At the gate. Padmini still in the saddle; Nagoji mounted just behind her, in boots. A Nair guard (as in 1.5) bows his head to Padmini, but his eyes have already slid past her to Nagoji.

copy.speaker: GUARD
copy.text: Amma. You come early.

copy.speaker: GUARD
copy.text: And this?

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: A rider from the north whom the sea sent back to us. The Maharaja plays with him. I thought Velinadu should have its share.

panels.description: Wide, inside the ring. The ground rises toward a central hall with a tiled roof, banners hanging heavy and still. Women along the verandahs in plain cotton and bright silk, heads uncovered, hair oiled and coiled or braided. Fewer men, in the same Nair dress as the guards: an older, heavy-set clerk with a palm-leaf bundle and an iron stylus (NOT Ramayyan: round face, greying moustache), and one with a sword, both glancing at a doorway where no one has yet appeared. Padmini and Nagoji dismounting in the foreground, Padmini drawing her long walking stick from the saddle.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: You stand in a place where land, not men, is the first thing named.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Do not address her as if she were a sardar's daughter waiting for a husband to give her meaning.

panels.description: Close two-shot. Nagoji, deadpan. Padmini (lined face, hair coiled at the nape, stick in hand) with a sudden flash of white teeth.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: If I forget, I expect you to kick me.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: That can be arranged.

panels.description: A stone side verandah, pillars, the red-earth courtyard beyond its step. Nagoji seated cross-legged on a woven mat, barefoot, his boots set neatly side by side on the verandah step, a brass tumbler of coconut water and a banana leaf parcel before him. Padmini beside him, entirely at ease, her stick laid along the mat. Behind them, through an open inner doorway deep in the complex, lamplight and the shadows of drummers thrown on an inner wall.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: They will make you wait. That is part of the weighing.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: My stomach had begun to learn this land. Rice instead of bhakri. Coconut instead of groundnut. Fish where once there had been mutton.

panels.description: Low angle along the verandah floor. A woman's bare feet, a gold anklet, the hem of a deep indigo sari shot with gold, stepping onto the stone. In the background, out of focus, Nagoji's back straightening, the tumbler halfway to his mouth.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Waiting is familiar to any soldier. This was the other kind.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The waiting men endure when summoned before someone who can change their fate with a word.

panels.description: Large, two thirds of the page. Revathi Bayi on the verandah, full figure, morning light through the pillars behind her. Mid-twenties. Deep indigo sari shot with gold, draped in the local style, the end over her left shoulder and covering the chest, her right shoulder bare. Gold armlets on the upper arms. A necklace of flat gold coins. A gold anklet. Her braid looped and threaded with jasmine. A thin line of sandalwood paste along her hairline. Kohl. No tali. Her dark eyes level and fixed on Nagoji, who has risen to his feet at the frame's edge, barefoot.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: She was perhaps a little younger than I. The way she held herself made her years hard to guess.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Padmini Amma. You come with interesting company.

panels.description: Two-shot, blocked left and right. Padmini at frame left: older, lined face, hair coiled at the nape, cream silk with a gold border, walking stick in hand. Revathi at frame right: indigo and gold, jasmine in her braid, coin necklace. Each gives the other the same almost-bow, the smallest fraction of a head.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Revathi Bayi. You asked to see what the southern winds had blown in.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: I brought him before the salt left his skin.

panels.description: Full width. Revathi turning her gaze fully on Nagoji. Over her shoulder (jasmine braid, coin necklace), his face, steady, taking it.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: She spoke Malayalam, each syllable placed slowly enough that even a northerner could not pretend to misunderstand.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You are the Maratha rider. The one the Portuguese could not quite break and the sea could not quite keep.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: So they tell me.

panels.description: Revathi (indigo and gold, coin necklace, jasmine braid), head tilted a degree.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You speak our tongue?

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I learn it. Slowly. Like a horse finding its footing on new ground.

panels.description: Tight on her mouth. A twitch, not quite a smile.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Good. Men who refuse to learn languages normally insist theirs is the only one that matters.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Those men bore me.

panels.description: Wide. Revathi settling onto the mat opposite his with liquid ease, legs folded under her, one hand gesturing him to his own mat. Nagoji still on his feet at frame left, barefoot. Padmini seated to one side, her walking stick across her knees. A servant, appearing as if summoned by thought, sets a brass plate of food by Revathi's knee. She does not look at it.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Sit. If you crane your neck the whole time, you will despise me before we have even argued.

panels.description: Across the mats, the two of them level now, Nagoji seated cross-legged and barefoot. In the background, behind Nagoji, Padmini (lined face, cream silk) rising quietly with her stick and withdrawing through the inner doorway.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You ride for Marthanda Varma now.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I ride where I am told. At present, that is for your king.

panels.description: Close on Revathi, tasting the words.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: My king.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: He takes heads when he must and lands when he can. He calls this kingdom his.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: That does not mean the earth beneath his feet has forgotten who owned it before.

panels.description: Revathi seated, spine straight, chin level, one hand flat on the mat beside her. The brass plate by her knee still untouched.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: You prefer the old ways?

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: I prefer ways that remember their promises.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: The Velinadu line signed pacts with foreigners long before your Maratha court ever saw a European.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: We bled when those pacts were broken. We killed when they thought our hands too soft to hold swords.

panels.description: Insert, tight. Nagoji's left forearm as he pushes the cream tunic sleeve up past the elbow. The Portuguese brand on the inner forearm, a hand's width above the wrist: a pale puckered patch of raised ridges, blurred past reading, no letters or numerals. A long, thin white scar along the inner forearm from wrist toward elbow. His nails healed but ridged.

copy.speaker: REVATHI (off)
copy.text: And you. What letters do you carry on your skin, Sawant?

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: A brand. Some scars. Joints that ache in the rain. Nothing a scribe would waste ink on.

copy.speaker: REVATHI (off)
copy.text: You underestimate scribes. They love scars.

panels.description: Revathi holding a piece of plantain between finger and thumb, not eating it. No bleed here: hold on her and the plantain.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: They say you trained the Madurai horse on wet sand.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You think you can teach our men to kill Dutch as easily as you killed Portuguese on your hills?

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: The ground does not care whose blood it drinks.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Yet you keep pouring. Why?

panels.description: Full width. Nagoji's face, hard, his sleeve down again. Bleeding into the panel edge behind him like a stain, not a clean flashback frame: a clerk's hand with a quill over an open ledger in a damp stone cellar lit from a slit window. The page shows only faint ruled columns and grey smudged strokes, no letters or numerals.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Because in Goa, they tried to erase my name and replace it with a number in their books.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I have seen their hunger.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Give them an inch of riverbank, and they will swallow the whole valley before you have finished signing their treaty.

panels.description: Revathi's eyes narrowing slightly. She eats the plantain at last, slowly, as if chewing helps her think.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: On that, we agree.

panels.description: Low angle. Revathi's finger pointing down at the verandah stone between the two mats, large in frame, the red earth of the courtyard just beyond the step, the two of them beyond it.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: This land belongs to my line.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Not to my husband, if I take one. Not to my sons, if I have them. To my sisters. To their daughters. To the name we carry.

panels.description: Revathi turned toward the south, past the pillars, where the land curves away beyond the trees. We do not see the sea.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Beyond the curve of the land, out of sight, Dutch ships rode at anchor.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: The company men thought if they pleased the right man, signed the right paper, they owned the pepper, the trees, the very wind.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Now they send different men, different papers.

panels.description: Taller than the other panels. Over Nagoji's shoulder: Revathi turning back from the south to face him, cool and even. Stack the balloons down one side and keep both heads clear.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Your king is not a fool. Yet he also wants to pull all power into his own hands.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: He builds a state that answers to the crown, not to the old lines.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: That is good for facing Europeans. It is less good for those of us whose names are older than his.

panels.description: Close on Revathi. A shadow crosses her face, there and gone. For once she is not looking at him.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: My mother's cousin sits in Kottarakkara. Savitri. Of the Elayadathu line.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: She writes to me sometimes. About the old ways. About what is owed.

panels.description: Wide and still. The two of them on the mats with a space between them, the plate barely touched, the banners motionless. Hold the silence a beat too long.
Revathi, recovered, her fingers closing briefly on the coins at her throat, then letting them go.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Kottarakkara has not yet bent.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Your king circles that house the way a dog circles a wounded bird.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I did not know the name. I did not know the house.

panels.description: Nagoji leaning in a little over his folded legs. Revathi does not move.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You fear he will use men like me to cut your houses down.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: I do not fear. Fear is for people who have no knives.

panels.description: Revathi pushing the brass plate aside with two fingers, clearing the stone between them.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: I see him giving land and commands to men like you, whose ties to this coast are thin.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Easier to shift such men when the time comes. Harder for them to say no.

panels.description: Tight on her face. She is smiling now, and the smile has an edge.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Will you say no, Nagoji Sawant, when he points you at a house that will not bow as deeply as he likes?

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: If he tells you my pepper fields shelter Dutch spies, will you burn them for him?

panels.description: Full width. Nagoji's face, unmoving. Behind him, one image only, bleeding into the panel in a treatment visibly different from the chapter's memory bleeds (desaturated, grey-washed, soft-edged, something pictured rather than remembered): dry Deccan black-soil fields of standing green jowar below flat-topped basalt hills, whole and untouched, and on the far horizon a single thin column of smoke just beginning to rise.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It was only a question. It landed like a thrown dagger.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I thought of my own family fields near Nashik, and what it would feel like to watch them burn on the orders of a king who called himself my protector.

panels.description: Medium on Nagoji, cross-legged, barefoot. He sets the brass tumbler down on the stone before he answers, his eyes on it, not on her.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I ride for the orders I am given. But I choose which king I allow to give them.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: That choice is not made lightly.

panels.description: Insert, tight and low. His boots standing side by side on the verandah step where he left them, the red earth of the courtyard beyond. No figures.

copy.speaker: REVATHI (off)
copy.text: You have already made it.

copy.speaker: REVATHI (off)
copy.text: You could have run north when the sea spat you out. Instead you stayed.

copy.speaker: REVATHI (off)
copy.text: Do not pretend you stand at a crossroads when your feet are already on the path.

panels.description: Nagoji, jaw tight, looking away from her for the first time, out at the courtyard.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Her bluntness stung because it was true.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I stayed because he fights Europeans.

panels.description: From beside Revathi, past Nagoji's shoulder: she has turned her head toward the inner doorway behind him. Inside, on a lamp-lit inner wall, the shadows of seated women, heads bent together.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: So you chose him.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Understand that you also chose to stand on the other side of some doors when they close.

panels.description: Wide, over the shoulder from behind Revathi (jasmine braid, bare right shoulder) onto Nagoji. Far back, through the inner doorway, deep in the house, Padmini (walking stick, hair coiled at the nape) a small figure half in shadow, listening. Balloons in the upper third; keep the faces clear below.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: They groom you. The Maharaja tests your judgment. Padmini warms your feet at her hearth so your loyalty tastes local.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You will be offered many things. Land. Honour. Perhaps even a wife from some house that can make you feel rooted here.

panels.description: Tight. Revathi's bare right shoulder lifting in a small shrug. Her eyes never leave him.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Not from mine.

panels.description: Nagoji, still seated cross-legged on his mat, barefoot. Nothing moves in his face.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The words were light. The tone was not.

copy.speaker: REVATHI (off)
copy.text: Men like you rarely have to ask. The world falls over itself to give them offers.

copy.speaker: REVATHI (off)
copy.text: I state my position early.

panels.description: She rises, smoothing her sari. He is still seated on his mat, barefoot, looking up at her.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Come. The others will want to see that Padmini has not brought a complete fool into our courtyard.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Then you will go back to the Maharaja and tell him Velinadu smiled at you.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Tell him also that we are still watching.

panels.description: At the threshold of the inner hall, half in its shade, she pauses and looks back over her shoulder.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: And Nagoji. When your horses trample that wet sand, they trample land that belongs to more than one king.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Every hoofprint has a name beneath it. Learn those names.

panels.description: Narrow strip. The empty doorway. Shade. A single jasmine blossom on the stone sill.

Padmini (lined face, hair coiled at the nape, cream silk) stepping back onto the verandah from the inner rooms behind him, letting out a slow breath, walking stick in hand. Nagoji still on the mat, barefoot.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: You did not disgrace yourself.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I am not sure she agrees.

panels.description: Padmini, looking toward the doorway where Revathi went.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: She does not have to. Her place in this story is not to approve.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: It is to remind men like you and the Maharaja that the land remembers longer than crowns do.

panels.description: Wide. Deeper in the complex, drummers at the open side of the hall, mid-beat. Nagoji, barefoot, following Padmini (walking stick) across the red-earth courtyard toward the hall. Inset, lower right corner: close on his bare feet on the red earth; behind them, out of focus, his boots on the verandah step.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: In Goa, I had fought men who believed God and gunpowder gave them the right to rule.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: In Velinadu, I had met a woman who believed lineage and land gave her the right to refuse.

panels.description: Taller than the other panels. Nagoji small in a big frame, barefoot, a figure between the gate behind him and the hall ahead, with open sky above him for the captions.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Between those two certainties, my own place felt precarious.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Yet there was a strange comfort in that.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: If storms had taught me anything, it was that balance is not found on flat, solid ground.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It is found on the shifting deck, in the moment between one wave and the next, when you decide whether to fall or to ride.

panels.description: Night. Oil lamps. The outer steps of the hall. Through a lit doorway, Padmini talking quietly with house elders. A male servant in a plain white mundu leaning in toward Nagoji, who stands barefoot on the steps.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: That night.

copy.speaker: SERVANT
copy.text: The Velinadu lady asks if your feet remember her verandah.

panels.description: Wide. The side verandah by lamplight, where he first saw her; his boots still standing on the step where he left them. Revathi standing, waiting, the coins at her throat dimmer now, jasmine in her braid. Nagoji arriving barefoot at the edge of the light, absently rubbing his left forearm, the sleeve pushed back from it.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You heard many words today. Tell me one thing you learned.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: That treaties are nets. And that Velinadu does not let anyone else hold the rope.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Not bad. And what did you learn about yourself?

panels.description: Nagoji, after a hesitation, looking out at the dark courtyard rather than at her.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: That I am still a man the sea has not decided to keep.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: And that I stand on land that can throw me off if I forget whose it is.

panels.description: Revathi's gaze dropping to his bared left forearm, the sleeve still pushed back: the long, thin white scar along the inner forearm catching the lamplight, the pale ridged brand beside it near the wrist.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: That one? Sea or fort?

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Dungeon. A Portuguese man with time and tools.

panels.description: Tight, lamplit. His left forearm: the scar along the inner side, the brand near the wrist. Her hand lifted, her fingertip hovering a finger's breadth above the scar, the brand beside it. The gap between fingertip and skin is the subject of the panel.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Travancore has its own tools.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Do not give us reason to use them.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Foreground left: Revathi on the dark verandah, her hand dropped, already half turned away. Middle: Nagoji at the verandah step, barefoot, turning from her toward the courtyard, not yet moving. Background right: the lit hall doorway, Padmini standing in it with her walking stick, and beyond her incense curling and old women seated in a circle mid-argument. Letterer: Revathi's tail goes to the foreground figure.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Go. Padmini will think I am trying to steal her new toy.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Where would I stand, when the king's wishes scraped against the houses of this coast?

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Old Velinadu women weighed the future in words sharper than blades.

frames.review_note: The correction works. v02 changes Nagoji's horse from v01's black horse with a white blaze to a bay: red-brown coat, black mane and forelock, no blaze or star. The lower legs are cropped out of frame. The rest of the image is unchanged, and the edit added no new faults. Nagoji still has the moustache, the clean-shaven chin, the rust turban, sleeves down and boots. Ibrahim matches his sheet, and Padmini is in her cream sari with no blouse. One small flaw is in both versions: Nagoji's visible ear shows no gold stud. It is tiny at this panel width, but a retouch could add a flush gold dot to the lobe. Older composition points the correction did not touch: Nagoji rides on the viewer's left, about level with Padmini rather than slightly behind her left side, and Padmini's side-saddle seat cannot be confirmed. The caption fits easily in the open grey sky at the top right.

v04 is clean. In v03 the bay horse had a white stripe down its forehead. In v04 it is gone, and the head now reads as solid ochre red-brown bay with a black mane, a dark muzzle and no white markings. At 5x zoom I found no seam, smear or tonal patch. A pixel diff shows the edit re-rendered a feathered rectangle of about x 442-788, y 299-647 (the horse, Nagoji's legs and sword, part of Padmini's walking stick, the hind legs of Ibrahim's horse). Outside the stripe, the changes are only tiny texture and tone differences (low-frequency shift of 12/255 or less). At 3x zoom there is no visible structural change and no hard edge at the boundary. Nagoji's face (x 580-680, y 180-300) is pixel-identical, with his curled moustache, clean-shaven chin and gold ear stud. The contact sheet at /tmp/claude-501/ch9rv2-sheets/page-01-panel-02.png did not exist, so I compared the two frame files directly. The single CAPTION fits in the misty sky at the top centre or top left.

The correction works. v02 changes Nagoji's horse from v01's near-black horse with a white blaze to a bay: red-brown coat and black mane, with no blaze, star or snip, even at full zoom. The changes stay on the horse and add no new faults. Nagoji matches his sheet: rust turban, a tiny flush gold stud, a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, sleeves to the wrist, the red sash, a talwar and boots. Padmini wears the cream sari in the old drape with no blouse, gold at her throat and wrists, the stick strapped along the saddle and the sword at her side. She looks ahead without turning, as the script asks. One older point the correction did not touch: white gate pillars stand behind the riders, although 1.2 already has them out on the road. Read it as a second gate. The three balloons fit in the open sky between and above the two heads, and the empty road in the centre gives more room.

The fix is done. Padmini is still mounted and alone, in profile, chin lifted toward the road with the faintest smile. There is no guard and no gate. She matches her sheet: lined face, thick black hair coiled at the nape (a few grey highlight strands, as on the sheet), gold ball earring, gold bead necklace and bangle, cream-and-gold sari over her left shoulder with the right shoulder bare, and the leather-wrapped sword hilt at her right hip. Her hand on the reins is sound. Her brown horse with the white blaze matches 1.1. The walking stick is out of frame, which is acceptable. The bright daylight follows on from the morning in 1.2. A large empty sky at upper right holds both balloons clear of her face.

Acceptable. A low red laterite wall circles tiled Kerala roofs and broad trees, with no towers or bastions. The gate stands wide open and is broad enough for carts. Two bare-chested Nair guards with high topknots, no turbans, white mundu at about knee length, spears and small round shields watch toward the viewer. No riders are in frame. There is no fort, no European building and no text, and the brass standing lamps on the verandah are traditional. Minor: the mundu hang just to the knee rather than visibly hitched, and the light is bright midday like 1.3 and 1.4. Clear blue sky top left of centre has room for the caption.
